# namespace2xml

> A deterministic configuration transformer. Reads ordered namespace profiles and structured inputs,
> applies scheme directives, and renders many outputs from one overlaid model. Identical inputs
> always produce byte-identical outputs on every supported platform.
>
> Version 3.0 is a complete rewrite against a normative specification written before the
> implementation. The specification is the contract; the code is an attempt to satisfy it. Every
> diagnostic carries a stable code and the specification anchor it enforces.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): entry point for automated agents; read order, repository map, reporting rules.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): the binding change protocol and the feedback report forms.
- [docs/specification.md](docs/specification.md): the contract. Normative, self-contained.

## Contract

- [spec/diagnostics.registry.json](spec/diagnostics.registry.json): canonical code-level diagnostic facts.
- [spec/diagnostic-stream.schema.json](spec/diagnostic-stream.schema.json): JSON Schema for `--diagnostics-format json`.
- [spec/contract-bundle.json](spec/contract-bundle.json): the revision `--version` reports, covering the specification and the registry.
- [docs/diagnostics.md](docs/diagnostics.md): every diagnostic code, its meaning, and its anchor.

## Usage

- [README.md](README.md): installation and a first example.
- [docs/usage-methodology.md](docs/usage-methodology.md): when to use this tool, how to layer overlays, how to specialize an existing document with a cross-format override, and known anti-patterns.
- [docs/migration-2.x-to-3.0.md](docs/migration-2.x-to-3.0.md): every intentional behaviour change from 2.4.0.
- [KNOWN-LIMITS.md](KNOWN-LIMITS.md): what is deliberately not covered yet.

## Formats

One guide per supported format. Each cites the specification clause behind every rule, and says so
explicitly where the specification does not settle a question.

- [docs/format-namespace.md](docs/format-namespace.md): the namespace profile — syntax, escapes, comments, references, wildcards.
- [docs/format-json.md](docs/format-json.md): JSON input and output — scalar kinds, strict parsing refusals, the numeric-map trap.
- [docs/format-yaml.md](docs/format-yaml.md): YAML input and output — the normative `RestrictedYaml1` subset and what it refuses.
- [docs/format-xml.md](docs/format-xml.md): XML input and output — typed components, attributes, CDATA, comments, namespaces.
- [docs/format-ini.md](docs/format-ini.md): INI output only — the two-level `PortableIni1` projection and its escapes.

## Integrations

- [ansible/README.md](ansible/README.md): the `stop_cran.namespace2xml` Ansible collection — two plugins over this tool. Which one to pick, requirements, arguments, memoization, and the four fidelity limits of the filter's data-to-profile mapping.
- [ansible/docs/specification-summary.md](ansible/docs/specification-summary.md): the contract in brief, and the only copy of it that ships inside the collection. Read this instead of `docs/specification.md` when you need the rules without the 300 KB. Its normative claims are blockquotes checked verbatim against the specification by `tools/check-specification-quotations.ps1`, so it cannot drift; where it and the specification disagree, the specification wins.
- [ansible/plugins/filter/render.py](ansible/plugins/filter/render.py): the `render` filter. Renders play variables on the controller and returns a string. Its `DOCUMENTATION` block is what `ansible-doc -t filter stop_cran.namespace2xml.render` prints, and is the authoritative argument reference.
- [ansible/plugins/modules/render.py](ansible/plugins/modules/render.py): the `render` module. Runs on a managed node, over files that already live there, and writes rendered documents to a directory on that node — idempotently, by comparing bytes. `ansible-doc -t module stop_cran.namespace2xml.render` prints its arguments.
- The collection is a separate artefact with its own version and its own compatibility promise. `v3.*` tags release the .NET tool; `ansible-v*` tags release the collection. The collection pins no tool version, but refuses a binary that reports no `contract-bundle`.
- Pick by where the truth lives. If the configuration is in your play's variables, use the filter: it evaluates on the controller and target nodes need neither .NET nor the tool. If each node's own file is the input and determines that node's state, use the module: it needs the tool installed on the node, and no file it reads is ever a file it writes.

## Verification

- [conformance/](conformance/): the portable conformance corpus, which is the independent oracle. Layout is specification Appendix C.
- [conformance/assertions.json](conformance/assertions.json): every acceptance requirement, its status, and its fixture coverage.

## Machine interface

- Run with `--diagnostics-format json` for the whole diagnostic stream on standard error as one canonical JSON array. Operational messages are suppressed in that mode.
- Run `--version` for `<field>: <value>` lines including `contract-bundle`.
- Exit code `0` means success, including success with warnings. Exit code `1` means failure.

## Reporting

- Issue forms: https://github.com/stop-cran/namespace2xml/issues/new/choose
- Route by asking what would have to change so this never surprises anyone again: the code (bug), the specification (ambiguity), the docs (usage gap), or the feature set (request).
- Set the `Component` field to say which surface you were using: the CLI or the Ansible collection. If a playbook was in the loop it is the collection, even when the message came from the tool underneath.
- Always include the `contract-bundle` revision from `--version`. For the Ansible collection, add `ansible --version` and the collection version; for the `render` module the revision that matters is the managed node's, returned by the task as `tool_identity`.
